title: Fundamental Rights
text: Fundamental Rights are listed in Part III of the Constitution, covering Articles 12 to 35. Article 21 protects life and personal liberty. Article 32 gives every person the right to move the Supreme Court directly to enforce Fundamental Rights. Dr B. R. Ambedkar described Article 32 as the heart and soul of the Constitution.

title: Writs
text: The Supreme Court under Article 32 and the High Courts under Article 226 can issue writs. The five writs are habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto. Habeas corpus is used to produce a detained person before the court. Mandamus is a command directing a public authority to perform a public duty.

title: Directive Principles
text: Directive Principles of State Policy are in Part IV of the Constitution, covering Articles 36 to 51. They guide the State in making laws and policies. They are not enforceable by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

title: Fundamental Duties
text: Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IVA of the Constitution under Article 51A. They were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. Duties are moral obligations of citizens and are not directly enforceable by courts.

title: Preamble
text: The Preamble describes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic. The words socialist and secular were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.

title: Basic Structure Doctrine
text: The basic structure doctrine was laid down by the Supreme Court in Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala in 1973. It holds that Parliament can amend the Constitution under Article 368 but cannot alter its basic structure. Judicial review and federalism are widely treated as parts of the basic structure.

title: Local Self Government
text: The 73rd Amendment of 1992 gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added Part IX. The 74th Amendment of 1992 did the same for urban local bodies and added Part IXA. Both amendments require regular elections to these local bodies.

title: Election Commission
text: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission of India. The Commission conducts elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice President.

title: Emergency Provisions
text: Article 356 deals with the failure of constitutional machinery in a state, commonly called President's Rule. Judicial review of its imposition is available to courts.
